title: Canonical composition and identity comparisons of pro-etale ring inverse image
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to Z$ be morphisms of schemes. On the small pro-etale sites use the base-change functors $u_f$, inverse-image functors $f^{-1}$ and direct-image functors $f_*$ on sheaves of commutative rings, together with their specified adjunctions, from [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Define the canonical natural isomorphisms $\alpha_{f,g}:(g\circ f)^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}f^{-1}g^{-1}$ and $\alpha_X:(\mathrm{id}_X)^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{Id}$ as the adjunction mates of the direct-image comparisons induced by the canonical fibre-product identifications $u_f\circ u_g\cong u_{g\circ f}$ and $u_{\mathrm{id}_X}\cong\mathrm{Id}$. Here the direct-image comparisons act by restriction along those identifications on every chart; thus these definitions specify the comparisons themselves, rather than choosing arbitrary isomorphisms of the endpoints. Use the same site universes as in [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image].
